question: A parameter is passed in the URL as /users/550e8400-e29b. What value should the in field have?

options.explanation: Query parameters come after ? in the URL: /users?id=550e8400. Here the ID is part of the path
Path parameters are part of the path template: /users/{id}. They are always required (required: true)
Header parameters are passed in HTTP headers, not in the URL

question: Your API has a GET /products endpoint. You need to add filtering by category. How should this be correctly described in OpenAPI?

options.text: Add a requestBody with a category field
options.explanation: GET requests should not have a body. This violates HTTP semantics and OpenAPI requirements

options.text: Add a parameter with in: query and name: category
options.explanation: Filters in GET requests are passed as query parameters: /products?category=electronics

options.text: Add a parameter with in: path and change the path to /products/{category}
options.explanation: Path parameters are for resource identification, not filtering. /products/{category} would mean a specific category, not a filter
Filtering via a separate POST is an anti-pattern. It unnecessarily complicates the API. Use query parameters
